title: A window procedure
description:
Dispatch messages to handlers with a table, and pass the rest to a default procedure.

```
WM_CREATE  -> onCreate, returns 0
WM_PAINT   -> onPaint, returns 0
WM_KEYDOWN -> not handled -> DefWindowProc
WM_CLOSE   -> onClose: asks first, returns 0 (window stays open)
WM_DESTROY -> onDestroy: posts quit
```
hints: In a real window, `WndProc` does `if (auto it{handlers.find(msg)}; it != handlers.end()) return it->second(wParam, lParam); return DefWindowProcW(hwnd, msg, wParam, lParam);` (lesson 1.04).
Not calling `DefWindowProc` for `WM_CLOSE` is what keeps the window open when the user cancels.
requirements: A `std::unordered_map<unsigned, Handler>` from message number to handler; handlers return the `LRESULT`.
Anything not in the map goes to a fake `defWindowProc` that logs it.
A quit flag set by `WM_DESTROY` ends a fake message loop.
stretch: Store a `this` pointer per window (as `GWLP_USERDATA` does) so handlers can be member functions.
